text:
Dubai recorded 10,379 residential sales totaling AED 29,532,710,915 in the last four weeks, a 2.6 percent increase in volume and a 7.3 percent rise in value compared to the prior period. Mortgage registrations stood at 4,047, tracked separately from sales transactions. The market remains heavily weighted toward off-plan inventory, which accounted for 59.6 percent of all registered sales during this window.

The median residential price per square foot declined by 1.2 percent to AED 1,677. This slight softening in pricing contrasts with the growth in total transaction value. Off-plan activity continues to dominate the market structure, maintaining a share well above the 50 percent threshold. The data reflects a steady flow of new registrations without significant volatility in the median price point for the broader residential sector.

Rental activity remained robust with 93,465 Ejari contracts registered. Renewals represented 50.3 percent of these contracts, indicating a balanced mix of new tenancies and existing lease extensions. The median annual residential rent held steady at AED 70,000. This stability in rental income supports the current yield calculations across various communities, providing a consistent baseline for investment analysis.

Investors should monitor Al Yufrah 1, which saw a 37.7 percent increase in median price per square foot over twelve weeks. Conversely, Palm Deira experienced a 13.8 percent decline in the same metric. Zaabeel First offers the highest estimated gross yield at 9.1 percent for flats. An anomaly monitor flagged 1,022 sales in the last 60 days priced significantly away from comparable medians. These figures are based on registered DLD data and medians, with benchmarks filtered to exclude bulk deals and outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
